learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and understanding of mathematics and other basic sciences inherent to their engineering specialization, at a level that allows acquiring the rest of the degree's competencies.

The ability to analyze complex products, processes, and systems in their field of study; to appropriately choose and apply established analytical, calculation, and experimental methods, and to correctly interpret the results of such analyses.

Ability to design, plan, and develop complex products (parts, components, finished products, etc.), processes, and systems of their specialty, that meet established requirements, including awareness of social, health and safety, environmental, economic, and industrial aspects; as well as selecting and applying appropriate project methods.
Knowledge of the application of materials, equipment, and tools, engineering technology and processes, and their limitations within their specialty.
Ability to effectively communicate information, ideas, problems, and solutions within the field of engineering and with society in general.
Ability to function effectively in national and international contexts, individually and in teams, and to cooperate with engineers and people from other disciplines.
Knows the characteristics of materials that have a different physical state based on atomic characteristics.

syllabus_topics: States of matter: solids, liquids, and gases
teaching_methods: Development, writing, and presentation of reports, memoranda, audiovisual material related to projects/POPBLs

assessment_methods.method: Individual written and oral tests for the evaluation of technical competencies of the subject
Individual written, coding/programming, and oral tests for the evaluation of technical competencies of the subject
Technical capacity, involvement in the project/PBL, work performed, results obtained, delivered documentation, technical presentation and defense

assessment_rules: The evaluation is continuous. Individual written and oral tests are used for assessing technical competencies. Projects and PBLs are evaluated based on technical capacity, involvement, work, results, documentation, presentation, and defense. Recovery mechanisms for each assessment activity are the same as the initial assessment.
